newsitem.title: FRANCE: OECD demands action on cyber child pornography.
newsitem.headline: OECD demands action on cyber child pornography.

text.p: The OECD, in a rare break from its muted agenda of economics and free trade, on Tuesday launched a strong attack on child pornography broadcast over the Internet.
The 29 industrial nations urged quick action to remedy the problem and officials said they had set up a meeting for July to compare national laws on misuse of the global computer network.

"Ministers ... strongly condemned the dissemination on the Internet of child pornography and information that promotes child abuse," the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development said in a statement after an annual finance summit.
"They urged that this abhorrent and unacceptable misuse of the Internet be addressed immediately including in the appropriate international organisations."

The condemnation -- the first of its kind from the OECD -- was included in a post-summit communique, mainly at the suggestion of Belgium, which has been rocked by a series of child-abuse revelations, diplomats said.
OECD Secretary General Donald Johnston said ministers at the summit had asked the OECD to take a "lead role" in helping to suppress child pornography.

Officials said the Paris-based think-tank would not get involved in monitoring the network or policing its misuse, but would try to help member countries regulate the web without sacrificing its economic potential.
"We want to put the facts on the table for all member countries to discuss," John Dryden, OECD head of information, computer and communications policy, told Reuters.
Experts from OECD countries will meet in Paris in July to discuss the results of a survey of national legislation to be launched by the OECD and to discuss further action.

The OECD's work already includes studies on how cyberspace should be regulated, though it has previously encouraged avoiding excessive control of the Internet and electronic commerce to promote free trade.
